reason: E2 supports that spark plasma sintering minimizes oxygen and yields a single-phase solid solution. E3 supports that intrinsic disorder in HEAs leads to low, nearly temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity. E1 shows that electronic thermal conductivity is suppressed by high resistivity but can increase with temperature, though it does not directly address HfNbTaTiZr or the specific temperature range above 300 K. The feasibility of separate measurements and the baseline conductivity range are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Oxygen contamination in HfNbTaTiZr can be minimized by spark plasma sintering of gas-atomized powder to yield a single-phase solid solution
Intrinsic force-constant and mass disorder in HEAs leads to low, nearly temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity
Electronic thermal conductivity in HEAs is suppressed by high electrical resistivity, but can increase markedly with temperature above 300 K
Separate measurement of lattice and electronic thermal conductivity is feasible using techniques like TDTR and electrical measurements
Total thermal conductivity of oxygen-contaminated HfNbTaTiZr is 10–17 W/(K·m) from 300–1200 K
